correctness.rationale: On real c0(I), I infinite, every sphere vector has a largest and second-largest coordinate modulus. Choose k with |x_k|=1, s=s2(x). For any y of sup norm 1, select sign sigma making |x_k+sigma y_k|<=1; for j!=k the same vector has |x_j+sigma y_j|<=s+1; opposite shifted norm<=2. Thus M_t(chords)<=M_t(2,1+s) for every -infinity<=t<infinity. A finitely supported y at k and a second-largest-coordinate l realizes both chord norms, with a separate explicit l when s=0. Any s∈[0,1] realized by x=e_k+s e_l. Gives exact full range/equality cases independent of dimension finite tests.
